title: Runes: a parse of a short text of a<a, repeated grows its memory about four times per doubling (1.5 GiB at 32 KiB), and withParsedFile gives no way to stop a parse that passes a limit
claim: At v1.1.0 the parse that withParsedFile runs (Runes/src/ast/parser.mts:144, retried at :149) grows its peak memory about four times per doubling of a TypeScript file of a<a, repeated: 181 to 185 MiB at 8 KiB, 458 to 460 MiB at 16 KiB and 1540 to 1549 MiB at 32 KiB, over a base of 82 MiB, in two runs. A C# file of int x = f(a < b, a < b, ... grows faster: 1082 MiB at 16 KiB, and at 32 KiB the parse aborts with Aborted() at a peak of 2152 MiB. Under a 1 GiB limit a process parsing 32 KiB of the TypeScript shape, or 64 KiB of the C# shape, is killed by the kernel with no output. withParsedFile takes no option (Runes/src/ast/parser.mts:41), so a consumer cannot pass the progressCallback that web-tree-sitter's parse accepts: returning true from it cancels the parse, and a probe cancelled a 64 KiB parse after 1024 bytes in 7 ms at 69 MiB. Runes already passes that callback itself (Runes/src/relations/extractors/kotlin-recover.mts:603).
evidence: Node v24.22.3 on node:24-trixie; npm install of @chrisdudek/runes@1.1.0, web-tree-sitter@0.27.0 and tree-sitter-cli@0.27.0; the typescript and csharp grammars built by buildGrammars at their pins and checked against their sha256. materials/parse-memory.mjs ran once per size under a 4 GiB cap, twice for each size of both shapes. Under a 1 GiB cap with --memory-swap 1g, TypeScript 32 and 64 KiB and C# 64 KiB were killed (exit 137), C# 16 KiB completed at 1024 MiB, and the cgroup counted three OOM kills. materials/cancel-parse.mjs with a 1024-byte stop returned null for TypeScript 64 KiB (27 progress calls, 7 ms, 69 MiB) and for C# 64 KiB (21 calls, 6 ms, 84 MiB). The commands and the printed output are in triage.md.
proposal: Give withParsedFile an optional options argument, and pass its progressCallback to the parse at parser.mts:144 with web-tree-sitter's meaning: returning true cancels the parse. A consumer can then end a parse that passes its own limit. A cancelled parse returns null, which parseFile already turns into an error at parser.mts:154, and the retry at :145-152 runs only when a parse throws, so a cancel is not retried. Separately, decide whether the growth is documented with the sizes measured here, or bounded in the grammar patches.
